So, what I've done is created for myself a fairly large Noise Library. It's much like LibNoise with a few key differences: I've named things correctly, using the correct terms; my randomness is better; I have a heap more modules and everything goes into at least 4 dimensions.

Mind you, mine is slower than LibNoise. And don't get me wrong, I don't mean to take away from LibNoise, LibNoise is fantastic, just didn't do what I needed.

So, with my noise library, I can combine sequential noise modules together (much like LibNoise). And that's basically all there is to it.

The weather does not move. It is drawn on it's own layer, so I've thought about rotating it differently than the underlying land-sphere. I don't think my noise library is fast enough to move things in realtime; however, I could conceivably generate the weather noise from 4D noise and loop the animation. But I probably won't because the math is hard and tbh, in a strategy game, you'll never be that close to the planet anyway :).

  • Rural land.

  • Silver, gold, and other precious metals.

  • A spade, to bury that metals on the rural land.
